sections.title: An operating philosophy in his own writing
sections.text: In his April 2024 essay about calm companies, Jackson describes a business designed to support both customers and the people doing the work. He links that aim to profitability, financial reserves, deliberate commitments and a sustainable pace of growth. His account of building Transistor with Jon Buda gives a concrete example: declining complex enterprise arrangements when the staffing and compliance demands did not fit the company they wanted to operate. This is Jackson’s explanation of his approach, rather than an independent assessment of Transistor’s finances or working conditions.

sections.title: From engineering to a consumer health business
sections.text: Tiny Health identifies Cheryl Sew Hoy as its founder and CEO and dates the company’s start to 2020. Its biography connects her interest in the business to researching the gut microbiome after becoming a parent. The same source records engineering degrees from Cornell University and prior experience building consumer brands.

sections.title: Why Mike King built iPullRank
sections.text: iPullRank identifies Michael King, known as Mike King, as Founder and CEO. Its company history describes his aim to build an agency around client outcomes and a multidisciplinary team. The agency’s published work connects technical search, content engineering and AI search strategy. Its founder archive provides dated articles and appearances for readers who want to follow how that work developed.

sections.title: From Meraki to Samsara
sections.text: Samsara’s investor biography identifies Sanjit Biswas as CEO and co-founder. Before Samsara, he was also CEO and co-founder of Meraki. The biography records a Stanford degree in Computer Systems Engineering and an MIT master’s degree in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.

sections.title: The operating problem behind the company
sections.text: Samsara describes its work as helping organizations use operational data and AI to improve safety, efficiency and sustainability. That positions the business around physical operations rather than consumer social media. Its leadership page separately identifies John Bicket as CTO and co-founder, providing a second source for the founding-team context.

sections.title: A research problem became a business
sections.text: The University of Auckland’s alumni profile connects Elizabeth Iorns’s Science Exchange founding story to her experience as a breast cancer researcher. She encountered difficulties finding collaborators and specialist research facilities outside her institution. The profile describes the resulting idea as a central platform through which scientists could find and outsource experimental work.

sections.title: Education and early company chronology
sections.text: The university records biomedical-science study, a PhD in Cancer Biology at the Institute of Cancer Research in London, and an academic appointment at the University of Miami. Its historical account places Science Exchange in Y Combinator’s 2011 program. The article’s leadership and financing details describe that period; they should not be treated as a current executive roster or valuation.

sections.title: Professional background and advisory focus
sections.text: AE Tax Advisors’ team page identifies Christina Nortman, CPA, as Managing Partner, Northeast Region. It describes prior experience at PwC and CohnReznick and work with owner-operated businesses and real estate investors. The firm records bachelor’s and master’s study in accounting at the University of Baltimore. Consult the current team page for her published responsibilities and the professionals assigned to an engagement.

sections.title: From solo product to subscription business
sections.text: Plausible dates Uku Taht’s start on the product to December 2018 and its paid subscription launch to 2019. Its company history describes Marko Saric joining in 2020 to lead marketing and communications. The business says it is independently funded through subscriptions. These are company-published accounts, rather than independently audited financial statements.

sections.title: Public professional role
sections.text: The company team page assigns design and development to Uku Taht and directly links the social account listed here. This verifies the published association; it does not confirm recent account activity.

sections.title: Founding Tally with Filip Minev
sections.text: Tally’s media kit identifies Marie Martens and Filip Minev as its founders, placing the company’s start in Ghent, Belgium in 2020. It describes a self-funded business focused on making forms easier to create. The kit links Martens’s professional social account directly.

sections.title: An independent software model
sections.text: Tally describes its European team as customer-funded and independent. Its public company page points readers to a product roadmap, user community and milestone blog, giving researchers sources for how the product develops over time.
